heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Steam coils with a short tube length of 1.1 m or less are:

options.A: Less likely to freeze if the steam trap is properly chosen and the coil is properly piped
options.B: Not recommended because they are more likely to freeze
options.C: More likely to freeze, even if the steam trap is properly chosen
options.D: More likely to freeze, even if the coil is properly piped and sloped
options.E: Less likely to freeze regardless of steam trap choice and coil piping

explanation: Short steam coil tubes (1.1 m or less) have less temperature drop across their length and resist freezing well when properly trapped, pitched, and piped.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: The purpose of the flow switch or sail switch used with hot water coils is to:

options.A: Stop the fan and close the outside air dampers if the low limit temperature controller malfunctions or the heat source fails
options.B: Increase the hot water flow through the coil if the outside air temperature is too low
options.C: Open the outside air dampers wide when the outside air temperature rises
options.D: Close the outside air dampers and stop the fan if the flow of water is interrupted due to pump failure or closing of the hand valves
options.E: Increase the heat source temperature if the outside air temperature decreases

explanation: Flow/sail switches detect water flow in the coil circuit and trip the fan and close outside air dampers if flow is lost due to pump failure or closed isolation valves.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question:
The use of ethylene glycol solution will result in which of the following:
1. Lower heat transfer rate
2. Better protection against freezing
3. Increased friction losses in the coil and piping
4. The requirement of a larger pump with more horsepower
explanation: Adding ethylene glycol increases fluid viscosity and lowers specific heat capacity, reducing heat transfer rates, increasing pressure drop/friction, and requiring larger pump power for freeze protection.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Steam coils:

options.A: Are installed exactly the same as are glycol coils
options.B: Do not require a vacuum breaker
options.D: Should be installed with tubes in a vertical position to ensure positive condensate drainage
options.E: When installed in the horizontal position, do not have to be pitched toward the return

explanation: Vertical tube orientation in steam coils promotes positive, unimpeded gravity drainage of condensate away from freezing air streams.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Air vents are:

options.A: Not required anywhere if a F & T trap is used at the steam coil
options.B: Not required on the steam mains if an inverted bucket steam trap is used at the steam coil
options.C: Not required when an inverted bucket steam trap is used
options.D: Required only with hot water coils
options.E: Not required at the steam coil if a float and thermostatic (F & T) trap is used at the steam coil with an atmospheric return and the steam main is adequately vented

explanation: A float and thermostatic (F & T) trap continuously vents air and non-condensables at the coil when discharging to an atmospheric return and the main is properly vented.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: The inverted bucket steam trap is:

options.A: Recommended when condensate flows by gravity into a return main at atmospheric pressure
options.B: Used when the flow is modulated
options.C: Used when the coil steam pressure is lower than 172 kPa or 25 psig
options.D: Used when the coil steam pressure is higher than 172 kPa or 25 psig
options.E: More expensive than the F & T trap

explanation: Inverted bucket traps handle higher steam pressures (typically above 172 kPa / 25 psig) and resist water hammer, whereas F & T traps excel at low-pressure modulating coils.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: It is good design practice to select a steam coil size so that:

options.A: It is twice the size that is required to handle the heating load
options.B: At least 80% of the coil capacity is needed when the air temperature at the coil inlet is -1°C
options.C: At least 40% of the coil capacity is used when the air temperature entering the coil is -1°C
options.D: At least 10% of the coil capacity is needed when the air temperature at the coil inlet is -5°C
options.E: 100% of the coil capacity is needed when the air temperature entering the coil is -1°C

explanation: Sizing a steam coil so that roughly 40% of capacity is utilized at -1°C entering air prevents gross oversizing and helps maintain steam velocity/trapping stability at light loads.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Glycol coils using ethylene glycol:

options.A: Do not use steam-glycol converters as their heat source
options.B: Are used only for heating purposes and are not used for cooling purposes
options.C: Use direct fired boilers as their heat source
options.D: Give reasonable heat transfer efficiency at low glycol velocity
options.E: Are not recommended for use in heating and air conditioning systems in the food industry

explanation: Ethylene glycol is toxic and not recommended for HVAC systems in food processing/handling areas where accidental leaks could contaminate food (propylene glycol is preferred instead).

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Steam coil piping and trapping:

options.A: Only handles steam and non-condensable gases
options.B: Can be supported directly by the coils
options.C: Is the same for hot water and glycol coils
options.D: Are installed in the horizontal position whenever possible
options.E: Differs from the hot water and glycol coil because it carries four fluids: steam, air, water, and non-condensable gases

explanation: Steam coil piping must manage steam, condensate water, air, and non-condensable gases simultaneously, unlike single-phase water or glycol coils.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: The flow arrangement best suited for hot water coils used to heat sub-freezing air is:

options.B: The parallel flow arrangement because it gives better protection against freezing
options.C: One in which the cold air enters the coil where the coldest water is flowing
options.E: The counter flow arrangement because it is more efficient

explanation: Parallel flow exposes the coldest incoming air to the hottest entering water first, giving superior freeze protection compared to counter flow when heating sub-freezing air.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Which of the following steam traps are preferred for use with steam coils operating at low and medium steam pressure?

options.D: F & T trap (float and thermostatic trap)

explanation: Float and thermostatic (F & T) traps provide continuous condensate discharge and air venting, making them preferred for low- and medium-pressure steam heating coils.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: The purpose of the "freeze-stat" temperature controller used with hot water coils is to:

options.A: Open the outside air dampers wide when the outside air temperature rises
options.B: Increase the hot water flow through the coil if outside air temperature is too low
options.C: Close the outside air dampers and stop the fan if the heat source fails or the low limit temperature controller malfunctions
options.D: Increase the heat source temperature if the outside air temperature decreases
options.E: Increase the fan output if the return air temperature is too low

explanation: A freeze-stat (low-limit thermostat) acts as a safety shutdown device that closes outdoor air dampers and stops the fan if coil/air temperatures drop dangerously low.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: In a hot water coil, which of the following is not included for providing a good guideline for the correct application of the system with minimal possibility of freeze-up?

options.A: Positive air venting of the coil is essential
options.B: The water velocity should exceed 0.9 m/s
options.C: A constant flow of water should be fed to the coil
options.D: The air velocity should exceed 10 m/s
options.E: The water temperature should be maintained at a reasonable pre-set temperature

explanation: High water velocity (>0.9 m/s), continuous flow, proper venting, and adequate water temperature prevent freeze-ups; air velocity above 10 m/s is not a freeze-prevention guideline (and can cause water carryover/noise).

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: To prevent freezing of the steam coil when steam pressure at the coil inlet is too low or is lost:

options.A: A two-position steam control valve is installed at the coil inlet
options.C: A second preheat coil is installed at the outside air inlet
options.D: Provisions are made to stop the fan and close the outdoor air dampers
options.E: A modulating steam control valve is installed at the coil inlet

explanation: If coil steam pressure drops or is lost in freezing weather, stopping the supply fan and closing outdoor dampers prevents cold air from freezing the coil tubes.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Which of the following statements about vacuum breakers is false?

options.A: Check valves used as vacuum breakers may be left open to the atmosphere
options.B: They are used to prevent freeze-ups caused by negative pressure in the coil
options.C: The vacuum breaker must be installed before the control valve and as near as possible to the outlet connection of the coil
options.D: Vacuum breakers are essential for satisfactory functioning of the steam trap
options.E: Check valves used as vacuum breakers may be connected to the return header

explanation: A vacuum breaker must be installed on the return/condensate side (after the coil outlet, not before the steam control valve) to admit air and break vacuum so condensate can drain.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Which of the following is not a cause of freezing in hot water coils?

options.D: Poor air venting of the coil

explanation: High circulating water velocity promotes turbulent heat transfer and prevents stagnation, so it does not cause coil freezing (unlike low/no flow, heat loss, or air binding).

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: A modulating control valve:

options.A: Is not used to control steam coils at any air inlet temperature
options.B: Is used for steam coils where the condensate is lifted to an overhead return
options.C: Can be used to control steam coils when the entering air temperature is above 1.5°C
options.E: Is used for steam coils when the entering air temperature is below 1.5°C

explanation: Modulating steam control valves are generally acceptable when entering air temperatures are above about 1.5°C, whereas below 1.5°C full-steam or face-and-bypass control is favored to prevent partial-load freezing.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question:
The greatest fears in hot water coil installations handling subfreezing air are:
1. Pipe expansively
2. Outside air temperature being too low
3. The failure of the circulating pump
4. Water viscosity being too high
5. The failure of the heat source
explanation: The primary operational hazards for water coils handling sub-freezing air are loss of circulating water flow (pump failure, 3) and loss of heat supply (heat source failure, 5).

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Steam coils with long tube lengths:

options.A: Are less likely to freeze than steam coils with short tube lengths
options.B: Are not likely to freeze at any temperature
options.C: Have the greatest freezing problems at extremely low temperatures such as -35°C
options.D: Have freezing problems at any temperature
options.E: Have the greatest freezing problems at temperatures of about -2°C to -1°C

explanation: Long steam coil tubes experience greater temperature drop and slower condensate velocity near light heating loads around -2°C to -1°C, where partial condensing can cause freezing.

heading: Types of Coils and Operation
question: Which of the following is not an installation recommendation for steam traps?

options.A: Locate the steam trap so that its outlet is at least 300 mm above the coil return connection
options.C: Base steam trap selection on the pressure difference across the trap and a minimum capacity corresponding to three times the coil condensate rate
options.D: Drip the steam supply main through a steam trap into the return condensate main
options.E: Install a strainer near the inlet of each trap

explanation: Steam traps must be installed below the coil return outlet to drain by gravity—locating the trap outlet 300 mm above the coil return connection would trap condensate inside the coil.
